title: The editor wraps text beside a photo, reversing spec rule R1 and ruling C2
context: The owner ran the phase 2 experiment on macOS and reported that text does not wrap beside a photo, and that the note stops scrolling when the pointer sits on a picture. Both the parent spec's R1 and the composer spec's C2 said the editor must not wrap, on the ground that no Flutter code wraps live text around a floated image and that the controller must never build a placeholder span.
options: Keep R1 and C2, and tell the owner the editor cannot wrap
Wrap in the editor by forcing the reader's line breaks inside the one text field with invisible placeholder spacers
Build the u10 segment editor, splitting the note across several fields so each beside line is its own field
outcome: Wrap inside the one field. The editor measures the paragraph at the reader's narrower column and forces each of those breaks by replacing the break character with an invisible box that fills the rest of the line, and it indents a line beside a photo on the left by making that box as wide as the photo. The drawn text stays the same length as the saved note and only whitespace is ever replaced, so caret offsets, copy and the saved text are unchanged. The measured Android hazard is a gesture recognizer on a span, not a placeholder, so the build-failing grep test keeps banning recognizers and a widget test now pins that every placeholder is an empty box. The note's photos moved inside the scrolling content, which fixes the scroll fault as a side effect. Beside a photo on the left the framework would draw the caret behind the picture, so the composer draws that caret itself.
